findings.heading: Iteratively produce tables for different levels of a variable
findings.proposition: The third indicator is the MEDIAN age of cases; the Russian text names it the mean/average age ("средний возраст больных"), while the chunk beside it computes median(as.numeric(age)) and labels the row "Median age of the cases".
findings.reader_consequence: A Russian reader believes the table reports an arithmetic mean age, misreads the printed indicator, and may reproduce the code expecting mean() where the chapter deliberately uses median().

findings.heading: How does R build functions?
findings.proposition: The Russian text states the function body sits inside SQUARE brackets ("внутри квадратных скобок"); the English says only "brackets", and in R a function body is delimited by curly braces { }, never square brackets.
findings.reader_consequence: A Russian beginner looks for or writes square brackets when defining a function body and produces syntactically invalid R, and misidentifies which part of a definition body() returns.

findings.heading: Why would you use a function?
findings.proposition: The English cross-reference carries a link target to the Iteration, loops, and lists page (iteration.qmd); the Russian keeps only the bracketed label with no target, so no link exists.
findings.reader_consequence: A Russian reader sees literal text "[Итерации, циклы и списки]" instead of a link and cannot navigate to the prerequisite chapter that this paragraph tells them they have already covered.

findings.heading: Testing and Error handling
findings.proposition: The English says the list returned by safely() holds two objects, the result AND the error it skipped; the Russian says the two objects "are the results" and separately that the error "is skipped", dropping the claim that the second element is the error itself.
findings.reader_consequence: A Russian reader does not learn that the second list element is the captured error object, so they do not know to inspect $error after mapping a safely()-wrapped function.

findings.heading: Testing and Error handling
findings.proposition: The English recommends stop() to make errors MORE detectable; the Russian says to use stop() "for OTHER detectable errors" ("Для других обнаружимых ошибок"), asserting a distinct class of errors that the English does not describe.
findings.reader_consequence: A Russian reader takes stop() to apply to some separate category of errors rather than as the tool that makes a function's own failures visible, and may not use it in the checks the section is teaching.
